content.text: {"conditions":{"rc1":{"status":"review","note":"The path from evidence to conclusion can be traced for claims 1, 2, 3 and 12 (S1 testimony, Privacy Investigation Report, discipline letters), but the summary never ties claims 4-11, 13 and 14 or the harassment conclusion to cited evidence, and the finding of no disclosure of Complainant's medical information depends on the privacy investigation interviews, which are only summarized."},"rc2":{"status":"review","note":"Many characterizations are attributed (S1, the Privacy Investigation Report, the July 1, 2019 letter, Witness 1 and 2), but 'undisputed evidence' on claim 1 has no named source, the discipline letters have unidentified addressees, the July 1 letter has a blank employee name, and the six coworkers' statements are not individually identified."},"rc3":{"status":"review","note":"Most events are dated (May 1 and 3, 2019, the April 2019 SPAR request, the July 1, 2019 letter, the September 4-5, 2019 discipline letters), but claim 1 shifts from May 2018 to Nov/Dec 2017, claim 14 has no dates, the review period is not stated, and the discipline letters are dated after the claimed events without any linked sequence of escalation."},"rc4":{"status":"gap","note":"The decision identifies its theories (disparate treatment, harassment) but not who reviewed the matter, and it does not address claims 4-11, 13 or 14; it also does not discuss the statements of Witness 12 and Witness 13, whom Complainant named, and the credibility discount for Witnesses 1 and 2 is stated without a documented standard."},"rc5":{"status":"gap","note":"An independent reviewer could not evaluate the conclusion without outside context, given the unaddressed claims, unidentified individuals and letter recipients, conflicting accounts of which coworkers were found to have improperly accessed the records, and the lack of a documented decision-maker and process."}}}
